findings.question: Q4
findings.title: An interrupt after accounts returns but before pending registration loses the handed spend and permits duplicate dispatch
findings.evidence_kind: EXECUTED deterministic source-line interruption, no owner or reader method replacement
smallest_reproduction: Build the existing synthetic battery ExecutionDesk with BudgetReader.following returning its live account dictionaries.
Keep an owner-created pre-execution BudgetLedger.from_dict checkpoint. Dispatch the admitted simulate_pulse action once; the executor settles the charge.
At the next pin, inject one KeyboardInterrupt with sys.settrace at owners.py:977. The accounts callback already returned and handed=True, but the mapping is not registered in _uncompared.
Catch the interruption, replace the owner dictionary entry with the checkpoint through normal dictionary assignment, and dispatch the same admitted action.
findings.actual_result: At both source lines 974 and 977, pending=0, unread={}, refused=false, executions=2. Source-line controls at 978 and 979 retain the spend and refuse redispatch with executions=1.
findings.expected_result: The interrupted handed observation must remain unresolved or retain its entry information so a later pin cannot accept a restored pre-spend account. An interrupted pin itself must not grant acceptance.
findings.trust_boundary: No private owner or reader state is edited. sys.settrace models a genuine asynchronous KeyboardInterrupt at an exact production statement. The execution side hands native dicts and restores a checkpoint using supported owner constructors and dictionary replacement. This is within the documented interrupted-handing contract; it is not an entirely unobserved spend/rollback between verifications.
findings.proposed_correction: For the demonstrated post-return gap, a local exception path can recover from the already returned local handing even when _uncompared registration has not occurred. Establish the exact callback/handing ownership transition before promising arbitrary-interruption continuity. Stronger guarantees across interruption of capture itself may require an execution-owner immutable handoff/acknowledgement contract; this review does not authorize that contract change. Do not convert a bare interrupt into permanent structural corruption.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Repeated interruption of native capture leaves a live mapping pending; checkpoint replacement erases its spend
findings.evidence_kind: EXECUTED deterministic fault injection at native snapshot boundary
smallest_reproduction: Build the same synthetic ExecutionDesk and dispatch once, saving the earlier owner checkpoint.
At the next pin, raise KeyboardInterrupt from _retain_handing twice: once during capture, once during immediate cleanup recovery. Restore the method afterward.
The reader now retains a raw tuple containing the execution side live dictionary in _uncompared, not _RetainedHanding.
Replace the live dictionary ledger entry with the earlier checkpoint and dispatch the same admitted action.
findings.actual_result: For KeyboardInterrupt, MemoryError and RecursionError, directly handed live dicts yield pending_type=[tuple], refused=false and executions=2. Identical detached-dict controls yield refused=true and executions=1.
findings.expected_result: An unfinished native capture cannot be treated as an immutable handed observation. Later replacement of the live mapping must not erase spend or make recovery declare the restored account current.
findings.trust_boundary: The monkeypatch only injects standard interruption/resource exceptions at a native allocation/capture phase; it does not forge results, mutate owner internals, or change comparison logic. Owner mutations are normal dict entry replacement and BudgetLedger.from_dict restore. The defect is the production fallback retaining the original live mapping after interrupted capture.
findings.proposed_correction: Distinguish incomplete native capture from a stable retained handing; never certify a later reading of its mutable map as the previously handed state. Local incremental retention can protect entries already captured, but cannot recreate entries never captured before both interruptions. A complete remedy may require an execution-owner immutable handoff/acknowledgement contract or a specifically approved unresolved-state policy. This is a design decision, not permission to invent another budget ledger or permanently label honest interrupted content corrupt.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Retained raw entry hashing bypasses owner normalization and permanently rejects an unchanged honest checkpoint
findings.evidence_kind: EXECUTED deterministic interrupted-read probe with canonical owner checkpoint restore
smallest_reproduction: Start a following BudgetReader over an ordinary ledger with one observed charge.
Append a normal settled charge with iteration=1.0 (or "1"), both accepted by BudgetLedger.settle and normalized to integer 1 by BudgetCharge.from_dict.
Interrupt the next _account read once; it retains the newly appended entry.
Replace the account with BudgetLedger.from_dict(account.to_dict()), an unchanged checkpoint according to the owner readback rule, then read it.
findings.actual_result: Integer iteration=1 control recovers. iteration=1.0 and iteration="1" permanently populate _diverged with "rewrote its history". _history(entries) hashes raw iteration while ordinary readback hashes owner-normalized iteration.
findings.expected_result: The same owner-normalized checkpoint should recover without permanent corruption classification. Any retained-entry canonical history must apply the same owner normalization as successful readback.
findings.trust_boundary: Only public BudgetLedger.settle and BudgetLedger.from_dict are used. No malformed owner state or private mutation; the API accepts these spellings and its existing readback explicitly normalizes them.
findings.proposed_correction: Reuse each owner entry readback/normalization before computing retained history. Do not advance _seen with hashes produced by a different normalization route.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Two interrupted detached handings permanently retire identical honest history before canonical reconciliation can run
smallest_reproduction: Use accounts() that hands BudgetLedger.from_dict copies of the current honest ledger at every call.
After the initial observed charge, append one ordinary integer-iteration charge.
On each of two consecutive pins, interrupt _handed once; immediate cleanup recovery succeeds and records its retained entries. The account content stays identical between calls.
Remove fault injection and perform an ordinary read.
findings.actual_result: Two detached interrupted handings permanently set _diverged to "rewrote the entries". A single detached interruption recovers; one or two interruptions with the same live objects recover.
findings.expected_result: Equivalent detached handings must remain unresolved until owner-canonical reconciliation can establish equality. Identity mismatch alone following asynchronous interruptions must not permanently poison an honest reader.
findings.trust_boundary: Execution side uses only normal owner round trips and supplies identical content. Fault injection raises an interrupt at parsing; it does not alter entry identities beyond the documented checkpoint-copy behavior.
findings.proposed_correction: Preserve unresolved detached alternatives until canonical reconciliation outside the lock can compare them, rather than writing permanent divergence from _note_unread identity mismatch alone. Retired-account skipping currently prevents later reconciliation from repairing the false retirement.
